local_checks.invariant: One idempotency key per logical attempt; fresh key only after a terminal DECLINED/FAILED or choice change; double-submit cannot create two distinct charges; polling terminates
local_checks.result: currentKey() sets keyRef synchronously, so a rapid double click replays the same key. The key is cleared on choice change and after DECLINED/FAILED, and kept on network failure or 503 (safe replay). The button is disabled while submitting or confirming. Polling stops at a 15s deadline and ends in pending or failed. The paymentToken is only a simulator label, not a credential. Server enforcement of key and course binding is backend scope.

local_checks.invariant: Idempotency key and choice state cannot leak across courses; the enrolled UI state is only UX
local_checks.result: CourseDetailPage sets pageState to loading on a courseId change, which unmounts EnrollPanel and resets the useCheckout refs. alreadyEnrolled is derived from the server's progress endpoint (200 or 403) and is not trusted for authorization; the gateway enforces access.

local_checks.invariant: A 401 triggers at most one shared refresh and one retry, and a failed refresh clears the session and redirects. The client has no path that keeps a revoked or other user's credential alive.
local_checks.result: request() refreshes only when the failed call carried a token (line 89). refreshOnce() shares one promise across concurrent callers, and the retry sets skipAuthRetry, so there is no refresh loop. A failed refresh calls clear() and the unauthorised handler. Rotated pairs are stored together. Retrying after a 401 is safe because the gateway rejected the original request. No client-side invariant failure with security impact found; a refresh finishing after logout can write tokens back (hardening).

local_checks.invariant: No real secrets committed; .env is git-ignored; required values fail closed
local_checks.result: .env.example holds only change-me placeholders and the non-secret GATEWAY_URL. .gitignore ignores .env and keeps .env.example. The frontend service uses no secret; other services use ${VAR:?} so a blank value is rejected.

local_checks.invariant: GATEWAY_URL substitution cannot be influenced by a request or lower-trust principal
local_checks.result: GATEWAY_URL is operator-set compose env (default http://api-gateway:9080). NGINX_ENVSUBST_TEMPLATE_VARS limits substitution to that one variable. proxy_pass has no URI part and no request-derived variable, so no SSRF or upstream selection from a client.

local_checks.invariant: Frontend exposure is limited to the intended port, with no debug or admin endpoint and no sensitive build output
local_checks.result: Only 9100:80 is published for the frontend. nginx serves static dist files and proxies /api/ only; no /debug, /env or /metrics locations. The multi-stage Dockerfile leaves only dist and the template in the final image. The healthcheck needs no credentials.

local_checks.invariant: Host and forwarded-header trust: client-supplied Host or X-Forwarded-For must not decide identity, absolute URLs or authorization downstream
local_checks.result: nginx forwards a client X-Forwarded-For chain appended with the real peer, but the gateway's RemoteAddressClientResolver ignores X-Forwarded-For and auth-service uses getRemoteAddr(); no backend consumer of XFF or X-Real-IP found.

local_checks.invariant: Edge security headers apply to every location, and no CORS wildcard or permissive config exists at the edge
local_checks.result: Server-level CSP, nosniff, Referrer-Policy and X-Frame-Options apply to /api/ and /; location = /index.html repeats them. No Access-Control-* header is set. There is no TLS listener (listen 80 only); TLS termination is a deployment fact outside the repo.

local_checks.invariant: URL-derived ids reach /api paths only as a single path segment, or the impact of a traversal is bounded
local_checks.result: courseId from useParams is interpolated unencoded in endpoints.ts. A decoded %2F or .. in the router param could re-point a request to another same-origin /api path with the victim's bearer. client.ts always prefixes /api, so the request cannot leave the origin. The victim's own bearer goes only to the victim's own gateway, the suffix is fixed by the helper, and bodies and lesson ids come from server data. No reachable state-changing target, no exfiltration to an attacker and no cross-principal effect found; recorded as hardening.

local_checks.invariant: Query strings are built safely; reviewId comes from server data
local_checks.result: CatalogPage builds its query through URLSearchParams and page is Number(...)||0. ReviewForm uses existing.id from the server's ReviewView for update and delete. No user-controlled URL text reaches the review update or delete paths.

local_checks.invariant: Anti-framing and response-header policy applies to every response, including add_header inheritance
local_checks.result: The server block sets CSP default-src 'self', nosniff, Referrer-Policy no-referrer and X-Frame-Options DENY with always. location /api/ and location / define no add_header and inherit them; location = /index.html repeats all four plus Cache-Control no-cache. XFO DENY blocks framing in modern browsers even though the CSP has no frame-ancestors. try_files falls back to /index.html through that location. No inline scripts in index.html.

local_checks.invariant: Host and X-Forwarded-For forwarding and caching do not let a client spoof identity or poison a shared cache
local_checks.result: /api/ sets Host $host, X-Real-IP $remote_addr and X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for (appends to the client chain; safe only if the gateway uses the trusted hop, reviewed in run-1). nginx has no proxy_cache, so no shared cache to poison and no /api caching at the edge. Host is not used to build URLs because the SPA uses relative /api paths. GATEWAY_URL is operator-set at container start.

local_checks.invariant: index.html is revalidated and static assets are not private-response cacheable
local_checks.result: Cache-Control no-cache is on location = /index.html. Hashed bundles carry default validators and no per-user data. /api responses carry no edge Cache-Control; any directive comes from the gateway (run-1). The nginx:alpine and node:24-alpine tags are floating (hardening).

local_checks.invariant: A navigate() destination derived from the returnTo query parameter must be restricted to same-origin in-app paths (no absolute, protocol-relative or javascript:/data: values)
local_checks.result: LoginPage reads returnTo from location.search and passes it unvalidated to navigate(returnTo,{replace:true}) after a successful login. All in-app producers build same-origin paths with encodeURIComponent, but an attacker-crafted /login?returnTo=<value> is attacker controlled and no scheme or destination check exists. How react-router 8.4.0 navigate() treats absolute or protocol-relative values is library behaviour not established from source. Other redirects use constants. RequireAuth is UX-only; the gateway enforces access.

local_checks.invariant: Tokens are cleared on logout, failed refresh and unauthorised redirect, and a new login overwrites the old credentials. A less-privileged same-origin reader cannot obtain tokens it should not have.
local_checks.result: The access token lives only in a module variable; the refresh token is in per-tab sessionStorage; nothing is written to localStorage. logout() revokes server-side (errors ignored) and always clears in finally. A failed restore or refresh clears; login and register overwrite both tokens. Only same-origin script can read the token and nginx sends CSP default-src 'self', so no weaker reader was found.
